Artifactory. Sensing and photonic engineering.

Explore the work through the questions it addresses: how to sense with light, and how to design the systems that make that possible.

Conceptual relationship between the work. Each project’s stage and evidence need their own assessment.
A company presented through its work.

Artifactory is the company behind the two projects presented here. The proposed positioning connects sensing technology with tools for designing photonic systems. It gives investors and potential collaborators a way to assess the work at a company level.

The site concentrates on ArtiSense and AIFIELD. Their pages describe different purposes, stages and evidence boundaries rather than a single combined product.

Related work, distinct responsibilities.

ArtiSense pursues a miniaturized chemical-sensing concept using photonics and signal interpretation. AIFIELD addresses photonic design and simulation, alongside a separate neural field research direction.

The internal glucose-related design example links an intended sensing objective to an engineering workflow. That connection does not make a simulated design a validated sensor, and the two projects’ neural subjects are not the same technology.

The supplied context describes optical feasibility and chip-design work for ArtiSense. AIFIELD capability descriptions refer to a September 2026 snapshot. These provide a basis for a technical conversation while leaving current availability and further validation to be confirmed.

The approach page explains how concept, simulation and physical evidence should be distinguished. Project evidence pages keep the limits attached to the work they describe.
